mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive in > 60% of instances where CPI YoY > 2%, or the correlation between CPI YoY and 20-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month signals a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns remain positive in > 60% of instances where UNRATE rises > 0.5%, or the correlation between UNRATE changes and 5-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a recessionary environment, leading to reduced corporate earnings and investor confidence, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain positive in > 60% of instances where GDPC1 declines for 2 consecutive quarters, or the correlation between GDPC1 growth and 60-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals a strengthening supply side, leading to increased economic activity and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain negative in > 40% of instances where INDPRO rises > 1%, or the correlation between INDPRO changes and 20-day returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an easing monetary policy, which typically leads to lower borrowing costs and increased investment, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain negative in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS decreases, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS changes and 20-day returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% in a month signals a weakening demand side, leading to reduced economic activity and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns remain positive in > 60% of instances where HOUST declines > 10%, or the correlation between HOUST changes and 5-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 6% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) declines for two consecutive months, it signals a weakening labor market, leading to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 6% and PAYEMS declines for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive in > 60% of instances where UNRATE > 6% and PAYEMS declines for 2 months, or the joint effect of UNRATE and PAYEMS changes on 20-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) growth is negative and consumer spending (RSAFS) declines for two consecutive months, it signals a recessionary environment, leading to reduced corporate earnings and investor confidence, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth < 0 and RSAFS declines for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain positive in > 60% of instances where GDPC1 growth < 0 and RSAFS declines for 2 months, or the joint effect of GDPC1 growth and RSAFS changes on 60-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).
